name: GHamine
summary: I build full-stack systems and measure whether their stated invariants hold. The three case studies on this site ship the fixture, the artifact path and the limits behind every number.

systems.title: Ledger Lock
bullets: Held 1 unit of stock against 20 concurrent buyers: 1 committed reservation, 19 rejection events, 0 oversold units across 3 seeded runs.
Moved the rejection insert inside the reservation transaction after commit 4f1c2ab left 2 outcomes for 1 decision; the seed now runs a forced-rollback case before each release.

systems.title: Merge Gate
bullets: Blocked 1 of 1 red pull requests and let 0 red merges reach main by making policy-gate a required check backed by rules stored in SQLite.
Fetches the head SHA at check time after commit b7d9e10 judged the previous SHA on a force-push; the fixture now includes that case.

systems.title: Citation Desk
bullets: Returned 12 of 12 answers with a resolvable passage id on the 12-question fixture, with 0 uncited answers shipped and 3 explicit refusals.
Replaced embeddings with FTS5 retrieval: 1 correct answer lost, 400 MB model download and 3 s cold start removed.

verification: npm run verify runs astro check, tsc, the asset and content contracts, the copy and accessibility audits, the JS budget, and a static build.
Every numeric claim links to a committed artifact under public/assets/<slug>/.
The site ships no client-side JavaScript and no tracking.
limits: The fixtures are seeded and small: 1 unit, 1 pull request, 12 questions.
The measurements prove the stated invariants hold on those fixtures, not that they hold at production scale.
The repositories are snapshots; the case pages do not call live services.
